report.lactate.title: Lactate and heart rate
report.lactate.lead: Lactate shows how hard your body works at each speed. Where the curve starts to rise is the aerobic threshold (LT1); where it climbs steeply is the threshold (LT2).
report.lactate.caption: Lactate (left scale) and heart rate (right scale) at the end of each stage. The shaded bands are the training zones.
report.zones.title: Your training zones
report.zones.note: Paces apply to a treadmill at 1% incline or flat ground outdoors. Hills, heat and wind raise heart rate at the same pace.
report.maxhr.title: Heart rate during the test
report.maxhr.lead: Speed increased step by step until you could not go on. The highest heart rate is your measured maximum.
report.maxhr.verdict_true: Heart rate levelled off at the end. This suggests you reached your true maximum.
report.maxhr.verdict_maybe: Not all max heart rate criteria were met, so your true maximum may be a few beats higher.
report.gait.frames_lead: Stills from the video at the key moments of the stride. What is marked is explained on the following pages.
report.gait.metrics_lead: Median values over all steps in the video, compared with reference values for recreational and competitive runners.
report.gait.window_hr: Running technique is judged on the film up to and including the first {n} stages of the max HR ramp (up to {last}), where heart rate was below 90 % of the peak, {hr} bpm. The last minutes towards exhaustion, where technique breaks down, are left out.
report.gait.window_count: Running technique is judged on the film up to and including the first {n} stages of the max HR ramp (up to {last}). The last three stages towards exhaustion are left out.
report.gait.window_warmup: Running technique is judged on the warm-up: already the first stage of the max HR ramp was above 90 % of the peak heart rate.
report.gait.findings_title: What we saw and what to do
report.gait.findings_lead: Most important first. One thing at a time: pick one cue and one drill and stay with them for a few weeks.

report.drill.overstride: Land closer under your body: raise cadence by 5% with a metronome, 3 × 3 min at easy pace. Also A-skips, 3 × 20 m.
report.drill.low_cadence: Run 4 × 2 min with a metronome 5% above your usual cadence, 1 min easy between. Twice a week.
report.drill.trunk_lean_back: Hill strides, 6 × 20 s on a moderate grade: lean the whole body slightly forward from the ankles.
report.drill.trunk_lean_forward: Plank and hip bridge, 3 × 30 s each. Think 'tall' when running, eyes 20 m ahead.
report.drill.pelvic_drop: Side plank 3 × 30 s per side and single-leg squat to a bench 3 × 10 per leg, three times a week.
report.drill.knee_valgus: Mini band above the knees: lateral walks 3 × 15 each way and squats pushing the knees out, 3 × 12.
report.drill.vertical_oscillation: Quick feet: 4 × 20 s of short, light steps thinking 'forward, not up'.
report.drill.ground_contact: Skipping rope 3 × 45 s and pogo jumps 3 × 15: short, springy ground contacts.
report.drill.hip_extension: Hip flexor stretch 2 × 45 s per side and walking lunges with an upright trunk 3 × 10 per leg.
report.drill.heel_strike: Barefoot or in light shoes on grass, 4 × 1 min: let the foot land under your body.
report.drill.stiff_knee: Run 3 × 1 min thinking 'soft knees', and do paused squats 3 × 8.
report.drill.crossover: Run 4 × 1 min along a line with one foot on each side of it.

report.tests_info.title: About the tests
report.tests_info.lead: These are the tests we run: what they measure, how they are done, which method is used, what you take home and where the limits are.
report.maxhr.not_max: The test probably did not reach max heart rate.
report.maxhr.peak_not_max: Peak heart rate in the test
report.maxhr.lead_not_max: The load rose step by step until the test ended. The max heart rate criteria were not met, so the highest heart rate is not necessarily your max.
report.hrzones.title: Heart rate against speed
report.hrzones.lead: You ran {n} steps of {min} minutes at an even speed. The heart rate needs a couple of minutes to catch up with the speed, so each dot is the heart rate during the last minute of the step. The line through the dots shows which speed belongs to a given heart rate, and it gives the speed for your zones.
report.hrzones.caption: Settled heart rate for each step and the line through the steps. Dashed line: outside the measured steps. The colours are your heart rate zones.
report.hrzones.incline: The speeds hold for a treadmill at {v} % incline.
report.zones.lead_hr_speed: The borders of the zones are per cent of your max heart rate. The speed for each zone is estimated from the relation between heart rate and speed in the steps of the test: speed from heart rate, not from lactate.
report.focus.hrzones_text: Stay in {zone} ({hr} bpm) on the easy runs. On a treadmill at 1 % incline: {pace} min/km ({speed} km/h). Outdoors the heart rate decides, not the speed.
report.gait.window_steps_hr: The running technique is judged on the film up to and including the first {n} stages of the test (up to {last}), where the heart rate was below 90 % of the peak, {hr} bpm. The last minutes towards exhaustion, where the technique breaks down, are not included.
report.gait.sync: Filmed at the same time as the first camera: {n} of {of} steps are the same steps in both films.
report.gait.uncertain_note: Uncertain: the film has {fps} frames/s. Values timed by the landing and the toe-off, and the angles in those frames, become reliable only from {need} frames/s. Read them as a direction, not as exact numbers.
report.chart.lactate_title.bike: Lactate and heart rate against power
report.chart.lactate_title.skierg: Lactate and heart rate against power
report.lactate.lead.bike: Lactate shows how hard the body works at each power. Where the curve starts to rise is the aerobic threshold (LT1), and where it rises steeply is the threshold (LT2). The trainer held the power in every stage (ERG mode).
report.lactate.lead.skierg: Lactate shows how hard the body works at each power. Where the curve starts to rise is the aerobic threshold (LT1), and where it rises steeply is the threshold (LT2). The thresholds are for double poling on a SkiErg.
report.lactate.self_paced_note: A SkiErg cannot be set, so the power of each stage is the mean power that was actually held in the stage (the first 15 seconds left out), not the target that was shown.
report.lactate.manual_note: * The mean power was written in by hand from the monitor, as the equipment did not give it.
report.drag.pm5: Drag factor {value}, read from the monitor.
report.drag.manual: Drag factor {value}, written in by hand.
report.zones.note.bike: The power is for cycling on a trainer. W/kg uses the body weight on the day of the test. Heart rate rises in heat and with fatigue at the same power.
report.zones.note.skierg: The power and the pace are for a SkiErg with the same damper setting as in the test. The heart rate zones are for double poling and should not be used for running or cycling.
report.zones.lead_lactate.bike: The zones are built on your thresholds from the test and are for cycling. Power is the safest guide on a trainer; heart rate shows what kind of day it is.
report.zones.lead_lactate.skierg: The zones are built on your thresholds from the test and are for double poling on a SkiErg. Heart rate is easiest to follow on easy sessions; on intervals power and pace are safer.
report.zones.lead_hr.bike: The zones are built on your highest heart rate on the bike. A lactate test on the bike gives the zones with power as well.
report.zones.lead_hr.skierg: The zones are built on your highest heart rate in double poling. A lactate test on the SkiErg gives the zones with power and pace as well.
report.zones.no_own_test: You have no max HR test or lactate test of your own in {sport}. The zones are therefore built only on the highest heart rate of this test. Zones and max HR from another sport are not used, because the difference between sports is personal.
report.maxhr.lead.bike: The power rose every minute until you could not go on. The highest heart rate is your measured max HR on the bike. It is usually lower than in running and is for cycling only.
report.maxhr.lead.skierg: The target rose every minute until you could not go on. The highest heart rate is your highest measured heart rate in double poling. It is lower than in running and is for the SkiErg only.
report.maxhr.lead_not_max.bike: The power rose every minute until you stopped. The highest heart rate of the test did not meet the criteria for a max HR and is for cycling only.
report.maxhr.lead_not_max.skierg: The target rose every minute until you stopped. The highest heart rate of the test did not meet the criteria for a max HR and is for double poling only.
report.trend.lead.bike: The previous test was on {date}. The same protocol and the same trainer make the numbers comparable.
report.trend.lead.skierg: The previous test was on {date}. The same protocol and the same damper setting make the numbers comparable.

report.focus.easy_text.skierg: Do most of the easy training below {hr} bpm, at about {load} W ({pace} /500 m) or easier.

report.focus.threshold_title.skierg: Threshold sessions at the right power

report.focus.watch_text.bike: The highest heart rate of the test was {peak} bpm. It is for cycling: use it for the bike's heart rate zones in the watch, not for running.
report.focus.watch_text.skierg: The highest heart rate of the test was {peak} bpm. It is for double poling: do not use it for the zones of running or cycling.
report.focus.ftp_text: Your FTP is {ftp} W. Threshold intervals are at {lo}–{hi} W (zone 4). Repeat the test after 6–8 weeks of training.
report.power.title: FTP and power
report.power.lead_ftp20: You rode 20 minutes as hard as you could hold. FTP, the power you can hold for about an hour, is 95 % of the mean power.
report.power.lead_ramp: FTP is computed from the ramp test as 75 % of your best one-minute power. It can come out too high for someone with a strong sprint: a 20 minute test or a lactate step test gives a safer value.
report.power.lead_best: Your best mean power over one minute in the test.
report.power.zones_sub: Coggan's seven zones in per cent of FTP
report.power.note: FTP is an estimate with an error of about 3–5 % and is not the same number as the threshold (LT2) from a lactate step test. The zone borders differ a little between sources.

report.followup.title: Against what the plan counted on
report.followup.lead: The plan counted on about +{gain} % in speed at the thresholds since the previous test, for the level {level}: {weeks} weeks of full load, with easy weeks and the taper counting less. The heart rate at the thresholds is expected to stay about the same.
report.followup.lead.bike: The plan counted on about +{gain} % in power at the thresholds since the previous test, for the level {level}: {weeks} weeks of full load, with easy weeks and the taper counting less. The heart rate at the thresholds is expected to stay about the same.
report.followup.lead.skierg: The plan counted on about +{gain} % in power at the thresholds since the previous test, for the level {level}: {weeks} weeks of full load, with easy weeks and the taper counting less. The heart rate at the thresholds is expected to stay about the same.
report.followup.lead_no_thresholds: The test gives no thresholds to compare with what the plan counted on, so this shows only how much of the plan was done since the previous test.
report.followup.done: Between the tests {share} % of the planned minutes were done ({done} of {known} min), and {qd} of {qp} quality sessions.
report.followup.done_unknown: There is no log of the workouts done between the tests. Read the plan in from the athlete's phone on the Training plan page, and it shows here next time.
report.followup.not_logged: {minutes} min after the last log from the phone ({date}) are not in the share.
report.followup.no_log: Workouts without a status and without a log from the phone are not in the share.
report.followup.extras: Sessions outside the plan as well: {n} ({minutes} min).
report.followup.estimate: What the plan counted on is an estimate from the research on how the thresholds move with training, not a promise. A difference of {tol} % or less is within the measurement error and counts as planned.
